label: r4c1
name: best recipe, lr 0.0015
hypothesis: Same as r3c2 (256 envs, 1 epoch, entropy 0.03), with lr raised from 0.001 to 0.0015. With 256 envs, early learning was slow (0.07 training success at 25%) and success was still rising at the end, so the budget limits learning speed. Larger rollouts should keep the higher rate stable. Refuted if the mean falls below 0.864 by more than about 4 points, or if a seed collapses.
last_analysis: Letting the target channels pass through a learned wrap-around convolution 1 row high and X columns wide is what made the task learnable. It took the start from 0.000 to above 0.76, while a dense mixing layer over each row reached only 0.42. Fewer PPO epochs, and so more fresh samples, helped: 4 epochs scored 0.77, 2 epochs 0.84, and 1 epoch gave seeds of 0.92 and 0.94. But 1 epoch with 128 envs left one seed collapsed (0.0 and 0.37). Raising to 256 envs (minibatches of 128 samples) with entropy 0.03 kept both seeds healthy, at 0.864 (0.90 and 0.83). That suggests noisy small-batch updates cause the collapse. These changes did not help: a deeper dilated trunk, a longer discount horizon, and a separate critic, which badly hurt. At the end of r3c2, training success was still rising and its early learning was slow (0.07 at 25% of training). So learning speed and stability now matter more than capacity. The traces suggest the remaining failures are a few cells placed in the wrong spot or in the wrong order.
